newsitem.title: JAPAN: U.S. Treasuries steady, undertone strong in Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Treasuries steady, undertone strong in Tokyo.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries were little changed in quiet trade at midday in Tokyo, retaining the bullish sentiment from a strong rally overnight that took the key 30-year bond yield below the psychologically key 6.50-percent level, traders said.

Traders will focus on U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony next week as optimism grew on inflation in the United States after the consumer price index overnight showed that prices were stable.
Traders said they expect no wild swings in the near term as the market remains cautious ahead of his testimony.

"The market will remain cautious at pricy levels ahead of Greenspan's testimony... The yield of the 30-year bond will hover around 6.50 percent as traders are likely to take a wait-and-see stance ahead of the testimony," a trader at a Japanese brokerage house said.
The 6-5/8 percent 30-year bond stood at 101-28/32, yielding 6.48 percent against 101-29/32 at Wednesday's New York close.

In late New York trade, the 30-year bond rose 30/32 to a session high of 101-31/32 and the yield dipped to 6.47 percent, its lowest since December 1996, after the June CPI rose 0.1 percent in a fresh sign of low U.S. inflation.

A trader at a Japanese bank said he will be watching Greenspan's testimony carefully as it has often changed the long-term outlook on U.S. Treasuries. But he added: "If his testimony gives no fresh trading incentives, some traders may take profits based on the '(buy the rumour,) sell the fact' principle."

The trader at the Japanese brokerage house said that, although bullish sentiment in New York carried over into the Tokyo market, trade remained quiet overall. Asked about recent talk of 10- and 30-year bond purchases by Asian central banks, he said he detected no such purchases this morning.
The September T-bond futures contract was at 114-23/32 at 0317 GMT, compared with 114-22/32 at the previous close.
